benefits: Real freehand drawing with pointer events — mouse, touch, and stylus.
Adjustable brush size and any color.
Exports your sketch as a PNG download.
Free and private — your drawing never leaves the device.

faqs.a: Yes. Pointer events cover mouse, touchscreens, and styluses, and touch-action is disabled on the canvas so the page does not scroll while you draw.
faqs.q: Does it work on phones and tablets?

faqs.a: Press the Download button. The sketch is flattened onto a white background and saved as drawing-board.png via a Blob-free data URL — no server involved.
faqs.q: How do I save my drawing?

faqs.a: Up to 25 strokes. Each new stroke pushes a snapshot; Undo pops the last one. Clearing the board also pushes a snapshot, so a mistaken clear is reversible.
faqs.q: How many undo steps are there?

faqs.a: The eraser uses destination-out compositing, which removes pixels down to transparency. Because the canvas sits on a white background, erased areas simply look white again.
The canvas is fixed at 1000 x 600 internal pixels and scaled by CSS, so strokes stay sharp and downloads are a consistent size.

drawing-board.formula:
stroke segment: line from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2)
with lineCap = round, lineJoin = round, lineWidth = brush size
eraser: globalCompositeOperation = destination-out
undo: stack of canvas snapshots (data URLs), max 25
howTo: Pick a color and brush size.
Draw on the canvas with your mouse, finger, or stylus.
Toggle the eraser to remove strokes.
Use Undo to step back, or Clear to start over.
Download your sketch as a PNG.
keyFacts: Freehand drawing uses pointerdown, pointermove, and pointerup events.
Round line caps and joins make strokes look smooth.
The canvas renders at 1000 x 600 pixels internally.
Undo keeps the last 25 snapshots as image data.
Downloads flatten the drawing onto a white background.
Touch drawing disables page scroll over the canvas (touch-action: none).

labels.touchNote: Tip: on touch screens, draw with one finger — the page will not scroll while your finger is on the canvas.

limitations: No layers, shapes, or text tools — it is a sketch pad, not an editor.
Undo history is lost if you reload the page.
Very fast strokes on slow devices can look segmented.
Export is a fixed 1000 x 600 PNG.

drawing-board.quickAnswer: A freehand sketch canvas with color picker, brush-size slider, eraser, 25-step undo, and PNG export. It uses pointer events so mouse, touch, and stylus all work, and everything — including the download — happens locally in your browser.
drawing-board.tagline: A free sketch pad in your browser.
drawing-board.workedExample:
Sketching a simple house:

1. Pick a dark color and a 6 px brush; draw the square walls and triangle roof in a few strokes.
2. Switch to a 3 px brush for the door and windows.
3. Make a wobbly line? Press Undo once — only that stroke disappears.
4. Press Download PNG to save a 1000 x 600 image called drawing-board.png.

No account, no upload: the file is generated on your device.
